sections.html:
Newton County lies east of Atlanta. Covington is both the seat and the biggest city, with Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle as the other cities and Newborn as a town. A city address may carry a city levy on top of the county bill. Interstate 20 and US 278 run through the county.

Growth has been steady: 62,001 residents in 2000, 99,958 in 2010, 112,483 in 2020, and 125,583 in the July 2025 estimate. Homes here are mostly owner-occupied, and a typical owner-occupied home is valued at $265,000.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
Pay in person at the Tax Commissioner's Admin Building at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101 in Covington, or at the Westside office at 3612 Salem Rd. Both open at 8:00 and close at 4:30 on weekdays, and 770-784-2020 reaches either one.

  • Tax Assessors, 770-784-2030: returns, exemptions, appeals and value questions
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and balances; an elected office, separate from the assessors and the county commission
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set the millage rates
  • Deed room at the Newton County Courthouse: copies of recorded deeds

Self-service kiosks stand inside Kroger on Highway 20 South and on Highway 278 NE. The commissioner's website also posts a delinquent tax list, refreshed every quarter, and a page on excess funds. You can mail a written balance request to the Admin Building. Include the parcel number and the property address, and say whether you need the figure for a closing so staff can date it correctly.

Newton County bills come due each November 15. That replaced the old December 20 date starting with the 2026 tax year, after the commissioners adopted the change in 2025. When November 15 falls on a weekend, the office has allowed payment through the next business day without interest, so confirm with the office. Real estate and personal property statements are mailed by September 15. Non-homesteaded mobile homes get a statement by February 1 and pay by April 1.

  • Late interest is figured monthly at prime plus 3% a year, with .0875% per month listed on the office's page
  • After 120 days a penalty of 5% of the original tax is added, and it repeats every 120 days up to a combined 20%
  • Mail counts only with a U.S. Postal Service postmark; meter postmarks are rejected
  • The office takes partial payments, but charges keep building on the unpaid remainder

Cards add 2.35% (Visa, MasterCard, Discover) or 3% (American Express), each with a $1.50 floor. An online eCheck costs a flat $1.50. Subdivisions that opted in to pay for street lights see a separate street light fee on the statement. The money the bill raises goes to county government, schools, roads and bridges, courts and the jail, fire protection, public health, parks and libraries.

The credit prints on its own line marked HTRG Credit and comes off the current taxes due before the total. For 2026, eligible homesteaded properties get an $18,000 cut in assessed value for purposes of the credit, and the dollar result varies by tax district.

Owners file nothing extra with the Tax Commissioner. The credit rides on an existing homestead exemption and sits alongside it rather than replacing it. It applies to the 2026 tax year alone.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, call the lender. The tax office has no say over escrow amounts, and a smaller bill may leave the mortgage payment unchanged.

Apply by April 1, or inside the 45-day window that follows assessment notices. One filing lasts until ownership or your primary residence changes, and exemptions never transfer to a buyer.

  • Standard: $4,000 off taxable value on county and school levies, one homestead per owner
  • Age 62: $20,000 off county and school levies, with a $15,000 cap on net earned income
  • Age 65: $30,000 off county levies and $50,000 off Newton Schools, with a $25,000 earned income cap
  • Disabled veteran: up to $126,526 off the 40% taxable value, backed by a VA letter

The two senior exemptions also limit household social security and retirement income to $99,648. To contest a value, write to the Board of Assessors inside 45 days of the notice and say which appeal route you pick. The Board of Equalization is one option. Base the appeal on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

sections.h2: Liens and selling with taxes owed
sections.html:
A FiFa is the lien Newton County records for unpaid tax, entered on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. A 30-day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before one is filed.

Once recorded, a FiFa lasts seven years and can be renewed again and again. The filing is public, so credit bureaus can see it. Settling the tax, fees, penalties and interest clears it. The office does not sell liens over the counter and posts a list when a tax sale is set.

Ask for a written balance dated near closing, then have the closing agent settle it out of proceeds. Statements go to the owner, not to the lender, so pass your bill along if a servicer needs it.

Gather three things before listing: the current balance in writing from the Tax Commissioner, confirmation from the assessors of which exemptions are active, and a copy of the recorded deed from the courthouse deed room if the closing agent asks for it. The buyer files a fresh homestead application, so tell them the April 1 date.

A cash sale can skip the lender's tax review and the wait that goes with it. Whatever is owed, including any FiFa, still comes out of the proceeds at closing. Newton County also publishes excess funds information, so a seller who is owed money after a tax sale should check that page. Settling an old balance before you list is usually simpler than negotiating it at the table, and paying it clears the public filing that buyers' title companies would otherwise find.

faqs.q: When is Newton County property tax due each year?
faqs.a: On November 15, a date that replaced December 20 beginning with the 2026 tax year. If it lands on a weekend, confirm the grace day with the office.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Newton County valuation?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the assessment notice date. Put it in writing for the Board of Assessors, pick your method, and rest it on value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption.

faqs.q: Will my Newton County homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions do not move with the house. The buyer files a new application, due April 1 or during the 45-day appeal window.

faqs.q: What are the Newton County tax office hours and addresses?
faqs.a: The Admin Building is at 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, and the Westside office is at 3612 Salem Rd, both in Covington. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, and the phone is 770-784-2020.

faqs.q: Which cities and towns sit inside Newton County?
faqs.a: Covington is the seat, joined by Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn. A city address may also carry a city levy, so read the whole bill.
